title: Coherence of canonical etale section comparisons
statement: Let $I$ be a preordered set, $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a diagram of schemes, $c$ any cone, $i_0\in I$, $G$ a sheaf of sets at $i_0$, and $W_0$ etale over $D(i_0)$. For objects $j,k,l$ of $\mathrm{Over}(i_0^{\mathrm{op}})$ and arrows $a:k\to j$, $b:l\to k$, let $r_a$ be the canonical section comparison [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison] for $D(a)$, and $q_j$ the comparison for the cone projection at $j$. Then $r_{1_j}=1$, $r_a r_b=r_{ba}$ (categorical order), and $r_a q_k=q_j$. No directedness, qcqs, affineness or limiting hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 03CB and 03CC, units of composite inverse-image adjunctions; applied to the comparisons in Etale Cohomology Tag 09YQ

proof.text: Expand the section comparison into unit, composition comparison, equality transport and restriction along pullback pasting. Unit naturality moves restrictions through units. The unit-compatible composition comparison is unique, and its associativity clause identifies the two routes for a triple composite. For an identity transition, compare with the identity-base-change adjunction; the unit equation and uniqueness make the composite act as the identity. Pullback pasting morphisms agree by their projections. For cone legs use the same composite calculation and cone naturality. This gives the identity, transition-composition and cone-leg equations, without a limit or qcqs assumptions.
